advances: Finite marked fibers with certified individual depths. Strictness uses one common intrinsic direction space. The location is a fixed graph mark.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
An ambient halfspace containing $v_i$ intersects its affine fiber plane in a closed halfspace containing the mark or in the whole plane. Its mass from that fiber is at least $c_i$. Summing over its graph atoms gives the non-strict bound.

For $n=0$ there is one fiber, so its mark has depth at least $c_j$, and the strict face condition is $c_j>\alpha$. For $n\ge1$, let $V$ be the common direction space. Under the orthogonal change of continuous coordinates into $V^\perp\oplus V$, regard the $V^\perp$ coordinate, which is constant on each fiber, as part of its base. The new bases remain distinct, and the fibers are full-dimensional in $V$. The change preserves both halfspace incidences and intrinsic fiber volumes. Apply 1ec728c26c11b368 to these finite bases and full-dimensional $r$-bodies, using orthonormal coordinates in $V$. This fact needs no convex compatibility and gives a minimizing cap through $y$ whose $V$-normal is a unit vector $u$. Write that cap on fiber $i$ in coordinates relative to $x_i$ as $u\cdot (x-x_i)\ge t_i$. Each $-t_i$ is the margin of the same ambient affine functional at the atom $v_i$.

Suppose the minimum mass equals $\alpha$. The retained atoms, with $t_i\le0$, have total weight at least $\alpha$. Each contributes at least $c_i$, so equality forces the mass of each such fiber trace to be $c_i$. A negative cutoff gives strictly greater mass than the through-$x_i$ cap, because $K_i$ contains a relative ball about $x_i$ and the slab between that cutoff and zero has positive intrinsic volume. Consequently $t_i=0$ at every retained atom. Every excluded atom has $t_i>0$. In particular all $t_i$ are nonnegative.

Let $F$ be the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}T$ containing $y$. Since $y\in\operatorname{relint}F$, it has a convex representation using every atom in $F$ with positive coefficients. For each atom $v_i$ in $F$, take small $\varepsilon>0$ so that $(y-\varepsilon v_i)/(1-\varepsilon)\in F$, represent that point by vertices of $F$, and average the resulting representations of $y$. The same coefficients average the margins at those atoms to the zero margin at $y$. Thus each cutoff of an atom in $F$ is zero, and all those atoms were retained. Their weight cannot exceed $\alpha$, proving the strict conclusion.

statement:
Let $z_i\in\mathbb R^n$ be finitely many distinct bases, with $n\ge0$. For each base let $K_i\subset\mathbb R^d$ be compact convex of affine dimension $r\ge1$ with intrinsic volume $V_i=\mathcal H_r(K_i)$, and let $x_i\in\operatorname{relint}K_i$. Put a weight $0<c_i\le D_{K_i}(x_i)<V_i$ on each $v_i=(z_i,x_i)$, where $D_{K_i}$ is raw ordinary depth computed in $\operatorname{aff}K_i$. Let $T=\{v_i\}_i$, and let $\mu$ be the sum of intrinsic $r$-volume on the disjoint lifted fibers $\{z_i\}\times K_i$.

If every closed ambient halfspace containing $y=v_j$ has atomic weight at least $\alpha>0$, then the actual raw depth $h_\mu(y)=\inf_{H\ni y}\mu(H)$ is at least $\alpha$. If all fiber planes have a common direction space and the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}T$ containing $y$ has atomic weight greater than $\alpha$, then $h_\mu(y)>\alpha$.
title: Halfspace depth transfer from a marked fiber graph
